providers.codex.nativeHive: Your Codex config has an MCP server named hive, reached over HTTP ({file}). Codex merges it into Combwork’s own hive server, and can’t start with both. Rename yours there to start Codex agents.
providers.codex.sandbox.default: **Set up default sandbox** (recommended): commands run under two local Windows accounts Codex creates for them (`CodexSandboxOffline` and `CodexSandboxOnline`), with a firewall rule that keeps them offline unless you allow it. It isolates commands best. Windows asks for Administrator permission once.
providers.codex.sandbox.needed: Codex needs a one-time setup of its Windows sandbox; until then it asks before every command.
providers.codex.sandbox.nonAdmin: **Use non-admin sandbox**: needs no Administrator permission. Commands run under your own account with restricted rights. It protects your files and blocks internet access in most cases, but Codex warns it carries more risk if the agent is tricked by instructions hidden in a file or web page it reads (prompt injection). You can upgrade to the default sandbox from here later.
providers.codex.sandbox.setUp: **Set up** opens Codex's sandbox setup, which offers two choices. With either, Codex agents in **Ask for approval** or **Approve for me** can edit files in their own folder (the project, or the agent's worktree) and run commands there without asking, and ask before going online or writing anywhere else. Combwork's own features (status, file locks, handovers, shared notes) work the same with both.
providers.codex.sandbox.upgrade: **Upgrade** switches Codex to its default sandbox, which runs commands under separate Windows accounts instead of your own. Windows asks for Administrator permission once. Codex agents that are running keep their sandbox until they restart.
providers.codex.storePwsh.fix: To avoid it, replace the Store's PowerShell 7 with the installer's, in this order. First uninstall the Store one (Settings → Apps → Installed apps → PowerShell → Uninstall, or `Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.PowerShell | Remove-AppxPackage`): while it is there, winget takes it for the same app and installs nothing. Then install PowerShell 7 (`winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell --source winget --installer-type wix`). Then restart Combwork and its Codex agents: they keep their old PATH until they restart. Combwork leaves your shell as it is.
providers.codex.storePwsh.label: PowerShell 7 from the Microsoft Store is installed
providers.codex.storePwsh.symptom: The symptom: a Codex command fails at once with `CreateProcessAsUserW failed: 5` (access denied), and works again once every PowerShell 7 window and command is closed.
providers.codex.storePwsh.warning: Codex agents' commands can fail while a PowerShell 7 from the Microsoft Store is open: Codex's Windows sandbox can't start that PowerShell while another copy of it runs.
providers.codex.stray.message: {folder} holds {files}, which isn't Codex configuration (config.toml, agents, rules) or a file it names. Codex treats the folder as its own, and stray files in it (an agent's scratch or logs) can make every Codex agent's commands fail ("setup refresh had errors"). Move those files out of it (scratch belongs outside the project); leave Codex's configuration where it is.
providers.codex.stray.title: A .codex folder here can stop Codex running commands

providers.copilot.updateModified: WinGet could not remove the old Copilot package. Its installed files may have changed since WinGet installed them, often because Copilot updated itself. Update anyway asks WinGet to replace them with --force. Stop Copilot agents first.

providers.settings.hooksOff: {source, select, inline {The --settings in Extra arguments} other {The settings file {file} (--settings in Extra arguments)}} turns off all hooks (disableAllHooks). Combwork's hooks are how it knows what the agent is doing (its status, file locks, what it is told) and they carry its status line, so Combwork doesn't start an agent without them. Take disableAllHooks out of those settings, or remove the --settings from Extra arguments in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.noValue: The last --settings in Extra arguments has no value. Give it a settings file or inline JSON (--settings '''<file or JSON>'''), or remove it in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.notJson: The settings file {file} (--settings in Extra arguments) isn't valid JSON ({why}). Fix it or remove it in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.notList: {source, select, inline {The --settings in Extra arguments} other {The settings file {file} (--settings in Extra arguments)}} sets {key} to something other than a list, which stops Combwork's hooks reaching it. Make it a list ([ … ]) or remove it in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.notObject: {source, select, inline {The --settings in Extra arguments} other {The settings file {file} (--settings in Extra arguments)}} isn't a settings object ('{ … }'). Fix it or remove it in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.tooLarge: it's over Claude Code's 2 MiB limit for settings files
providers.settings.unreadable: The settings file {file} (--settings in Extra arguments) can't be read: {why}. Fix it or remove it in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.unknown: Unknown provider "{provider}". It may need a newer version of Combwork.
